releases.body:
Adds an official keyless free tier for You.com via hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) `you-search`, enabling out-of-the-box search without registration or an API key.

### Added

- **You.com Keyless Free Tier (`osp-youcom`):** Without an API key, requests automatically route to You.com's hosted MCP server (`https://api.you.com/mcp?profile=free`) using Streamable HTTP `tools/call`. Users get immediate, keyless web search out of the box with zero configuration or signup required.
- **Dual-Tier Dynamic Routing:** Configuring `OSP_YDC_API_KEY` (or connecting via `/connect`) transparently upgrades requests to You.com's dedicated commercial REST API (`https://ydc-index.io/v1/search`) with higher rate limits and paid quota.
- **Host Override Metadata:** Passed `YOUCOM_LANGUAGE` and `YOUCOM_COUNTRY` via `params._meta["com.you.com/search"]` in keyless MCP requests, ensuring search localization works properly in both free and keyed modes.
- **Robust SSE & MCP Parser:** Built-in lightweight SSE stream parser supporting multi-line `data:` framing, `result.isError` error handling, and JSON-RPC error envelope reporting.
- **Keyless Pool Integration:** You.com joins AnySearch and Keenable as an always-available provider in OpenCode's search pool, with clear HTTP 429 upgrade guidance when free daily limits are reached.

### How to use

No configuration needed! You.com is now available immediately upon installing the plugin:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "websearch": { "provider": "osp-youcom" }
}
```

Or set `"provider": "random"` to include You.com in the provider rotation pool. If you have a commercial You.com API key, provide `OSP_YDC_API_KEY` in environment or configure it in `/connect` to use your dedicated allowance.

### Changed

- Updated `README.md` and `README.zh-CN.md` to list You.com alongside AnySearch and Keenable as anonymous/keyless providers.
- Updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` and structure test suites to reflect You.com's keyless tier status.

### Validation

- TypeScript checks (`tsc --noEmit`) and all 35 test files passed (**857 tests passed, 3 skipped**).
- Structure tests verify zero cross-file imports and byte-identical shared block consistency across all providers.
- Live end-to-end verification against `https://api.you.com/mcp?profile=free` confirmed Chinese, English, special character, and localized query handling.
- Bilingual README audit (`node scripts/audit-readme.mjs`) passed.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/guotree/opencode-search-plugin/compare/v4.7.0...v4.7.1

Adds Zhipu Coding Plan and Z.ai Coding Plan Remote MCP search (`web_search_prime`), bringing the plugin to 24 search providers.

### Added

- **Zhipu Coding Plan (`osp-zhipu-coding`):** Remote MCP search on Zhipu's cn platform (`open.bigmodel.cn`). Consumes plan shared credits (1.2 credits/call) with Streamable HTTP sessions, protocol version negotiation, JSON and SSE replies, and schema-driven parameters.
- **Z.ai Coding Plan (`osp-zai-coding`):** Remote MCP search on Z.ai's international platform (`api.z.ai`). Completely separate credentials and endpoints from the metered REST search (`osp-zai`).
- **Streamable HTTP MCP Client:** One cache miss performs `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, and a best-effort `DELETE` under one unified deadline (`*_TIMEOUT`, default 25s). Session cleanup has its own 1s timeout to ensure search results are never delayed or masked by slow teardown.
- **Security & Redaction:** Credentials (`apiKey`, `Bearer <key>`) and session IDs are strictly redacted from error messages. Cache keys are partitioned with a 64-bit dual-hash fingerprint and request parameters.
- **Typed HTTP 429 Contract:** Preserves OpenCode's typed rate-limit error contract and `Retry-After` header so host-level `random` failover and provider cooldowns work out of the box.

### Get started

Connect **Zhipu Coding Plan (osp)** or **Z.ai Coding Plan (osp)** through `/connect`, or configure environment variables:
- `OSP_ZHIPU_CODING_API_KEY`: Key from [bigmodel.cn](https://bigmodel.cn/apikey/coding-plan-per)
- `OSP_ZAI_CODING_API_KEY`: Key from [z.ai](https://z.ai/manage-apikey/apikey-list)

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "websearch": { "provider": "osp-zhipu-coding" }
}
```

Or set `"provider": "random"` to include Coding Plan search in the available provider pool.

### Changed

- Both READMEs now document configuration, shared credit usage, and troubleshooting for Coding Plan authentication and policy errors.
- Documented the shared `trimContent` block in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### Validation

- TypeScript checks and all 35 test files passed (**850 tests passed, 2 skipped**).
- Structure tests verify zero cross-file imports and byte-identical shared MCP session client blocks.
- Bilingual README audit and package-content checks (`npm pack --dry-run`) passed.

### Limitations & Policy Notice

Both providers are marked **experimental**: official plan documentation describes use by compatible MCP clients but does not explicitly name this plugin as an officially supported client; no live Coding Plan key or billing account has been used to verify the integration.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/guotree/opencode-search-plugin/compare/v4.6.1...v4.7.0

Fixes rate-limit failover and request cancellation across all 22 search adapters, plus You.com's empty-content fallback.

- Preserve OpenCode's typed HTTP 429 contract and `Retry-After` so `random` selection can switch providers and apply cooldowns. Error metadata uses credential-free endpoints; failed or stalled 429 response bodies retain their throttle classification. Authentication, payment and policy failures keep their existing meaning.
- Keep request cancellation active through response-body reading, including with `*_TIMEOUT=0`. Scoped controllers stop unfinished downloads on exit, body timeouts retain the correct diagnosis, and cache hits do not allocate controllers.
- Skip empty or whitespace-only You.com highlights, Markdown and snippets when choosing fallback content, preserving the selected text's formatting without additional requests.

Validation: TypeScript checks and all 33 test files passed (785 tests passed, 2 expected skips). Local HTTP checks confirmed cancellation closes the connection. An isolated OpenCode 2.2.5 host with simulated upstream responses verified random failover, cooldown exclusion, fixed-provider failures, authentication failure termination and exhausted-pool termination. Bilingual README audit and package-content checks passed.

No provider IDs, credential variable names or request parameters changed.

Adds Tencent Yuanbao Search as `osp-yuanbao`, bringing the plugin to 22 search providers. The default request sends only `Query`, so lite accounts can search without unsupported parameters.

### Added

- **Yuanbao Search:** Bearer service-key authentication with optional result count, site, calendar freshness and industry filters. The account tier is selected in the Tencent Cloud console; all tiers share one endpoint.
- **Result handling:** Decodes JSON-string pages independently, keeps usable sources when another row is malformed, and prefers dynamic excerpts over standard excerpts. Dates without an explicit timezone are omitted.
- **Rate-limit failover:** Both HTTP 429 and the `RequestLimitExceeded` business error use OpenCode's typed throttle contract, preserving `Retry-After` and the real upstream status in diagnostics. HTTP 200 business errors and known policy refusals are reported without caching them as empty results.

### Get started

Connect **Yuanbao Search (osp)** through `/connect`, or provide `OSP_YUANBAO_API_KEY` in the OpenCode server's environment. Use a service API key from the [Yuanbao Search console](https://console.cloud.tencent.com/wsapi/index?tab=apikey).

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "websearch": { "provider": "osp-yuanbao" }
}
```

Use `"random"` instead to include Yuanbao in the available provider pool. A saved `/connect` credential takes precedence over the environment variable.

### Changed

- Both READMEs now cover setup, tier restrictions, credential precedence, environment inheritance and HTTP 200 business-error troubleshooting.
- Random selection is documented as keeping the same provider within a session. Automatic failover depends on the adapter preserving the host's typed HTTP 429 error contract.

### Validation

- TypeScript check passed; **496 tests passed, 2 skipped**. Bilingual README audit and package-content checks passed.
- Valid-key lite checks on 2026-11-02 returned **40 results across four queries**: Chinese, English, a site filter and `d7` freshness. All 10 site-filtered results matched the requested domain; sampled freshness dates were within the requested window. All four repeated queries used the local cache.
- HTTP 429 and business-throttle failover, terminal authentication errors and fixed-provider behavior were verified in an isolated **OpenCode 2.2.5** instance using simulated upstream responses.

### Limitations

Standard/flagship responses, domain exclusions, result-count and industry filters remain unverified against the live service. Lite accounts should leave `YUANBAO_COUNT` and `YUANBAO_INDUSTRY` unset. The live checks verify basic behavior and do not establish overall retrieval quality or latency guarantees.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/guotree/opencode-search-plugin/compare/v4.5.0...v4.6.0

> **Behavior change:** Moonshot, Moonshot CN and Jina now cut each hit's body to `*_CONTENT_CHARS` code points whenever content is read, so the result and the cache hold an already-clipped page. A configuration that explicitly sets `<PROVIDER>_INCLUDE_CONTENT` (`MOONSHOT_INCLUDE_CONTENT`, `MOONSHOT_CN_INCLUDE_CONTENT`, `JINA_INCLUDE_CONTENT`) and needs the whole page must now opt out with `<PROVIDER>_CONTENT_CHARS=0`; the default is no longer "everything the vendor returned". The same per-hit limit also applies to snippets, even when full-page content is disabled.

### Fixed

- **Full-page bodies are bounded before they reach the agent and its cache** (Moonshot, Moonshot CN, Jina). With `*_INCLUDE_CONTENT` on, each hit's body was mapped into the result and cached whole: a Moonshot `text` or a Jina markdown page can run to hundreds of kilobytes, and the 200-entry cache kept every copy, so the memory cost followed the context cost. `MOONSHOT_CONTENT_CHARS`, `MOONSHOT_CN_CONTENT_CHARS` and `JINA_CONTENT_CHARS` (all default `4000`) now cut each body to code points before the result is returned and therefore before `writeCache` stores it; `0` disables this per-hit truncation. The limit produces a preview that may omit relevant passages; it does not cap total search output, token usage, or response download and parsing memory. The cut counts code points, so no surrogate pair is sliced, and the trailing ellipsis marks clipped content. `test/structure.test.ts` asserts the shared `trimContent` block, that every listed file applies it, and that files with no full-page body carry no `CONTENT_CHARS` knob. Each provider's test covers the default, `0`, surrogate pairs, and the cached copy. Metaso (`rawContent`) and You.com (`full_page`) can return whole pages too and are not covered by this change.

### Changed

- Both READMEs now distinguish per-hit previews from total output budgets, explain that search providers are independent of the consuming model, and qualify observations from the recorded Ollama and Linkup samples.

**Validation:** TypeScript check passed; 432 tests passed, 2 skipped; bilingual README audit passed.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/guotree/opencode-search-plugin/compare/v4.4.1...v4.5.0
